quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Listen for what changes between the waiting room and the end of the speech.
quests.explanation: The nerves came before; by the end the ordeal is over and the speaker can relax. That's what the clues add up to: relief.
quests.textToSpeak: So, that's done. I was terrified in the waiting room, but once I started talking, it was fine. Now I just want a very large sandwich.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: How does the speaker's mood change after the second sentence?
quests.explanation: The good mood collapses when the plan falls through. The lasting feeling is disappointment.
quests.textToSpeak: The train pulled in right on time, and I felt fantastic. Then they told me our seats had been double-booked, and we'd have to wait for the next one.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What has changed between the crying and this morning?
quests.explanation: The sadness has faded into a settled sense of belonging. Everything points to contentment.
quests.textToSpeak: I cried a lot after the move. But this morning I woke up, made coffee, and the apartment felt like mine for the first time.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What does the second half of the email do to the first?
quests.explanation: Hope built up by the friendly opening is undone by the rejection.
quests.textToSpeak: I thought this was going to be the year. I really did. The email started so nicely, 'We were very impressed,' and then it explained why they were going with someone else.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What has the speaker decided?
quests.explanation: Anger has burned out, and the speaker decides to stop fighting. So resigned is the best fit.
quests.textToSpeak: I argued with them for an hour. I wrote a complaint. Now it's midnight, and I've decided it isn't worth another minute. They can keep the money.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: How does the situation change in the last sentence?
quests.explanation: The danger is gone, and the speaker's tension goes with it. That's what the clues add up to: relief.
quests.textToSpeak: The lights flickered, the wind was howling, and I'd already packed a bag. Then the power came back, and the radio said the worst had passed.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: How does the speaker's plan compare with what actually happened?
quests.explanation: The dreaded conversation turns out to need no explanation. The speaker's tension lifts. That's relief.
quests.textToSpeak: I had a whole plan for how to break the news to him. Then he looked at me and said, 'I already knew.' We just sat there for a minute.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Where is the speaker looking, and why?
quests.explanation: Pleasure may be underneath, but looking away from everyone shows that discomfort at the attention is strongest. The speaker is embarrassed.
quests.textToSpeak: For weeks I thought nobody had noticed my work. Then the CEO mentioned it in her closing speech, by name. I looked at my shoes the whole time.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What did the speaker expect, and what did they get?
quests.explanation: The speaker was thrown by an unexpected response. Surprise is the feeling here.
quests.textToSpeak: I was ready for an argument. He listened to the whole thing, nodded, and said, 'You're right.' I honestly didn't know what to do with my hands.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Whose work is being praised, and who is being ignored?
quests.explanation: The speaker is receiving credit that belongs partly to someone else. Everything points to guilt.
quests.textToSpeak: They all clapped when I was thanked for the project. But half of it was Mia's work, and she was standing right there, saying nothing.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Focus on what the speaker says means more than the grade.
quests.explanation: The speaker recognizes an undeserved kindness and values it. Gratitude is the feeling here.
quests.textToSpeak: I know I don't deserve the extension. I was late through my own fault. But you gave it anyway, and that means more to me than the grade.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What can the speaker do now that they couldn't do before?
quests.explanation: Confessing removes the weight, and the speaker can face people again. Everything points to relief.
quests.textToSpeak: I told them the truth about the mistake this morning. My stomach hurt for hours before, but now it's off my chest, and I can look at my colleagues again.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What does the speaker actually do when she wins?
quests.explanation: The jealous thought is honest, but the speaker's actions show they're proud of her.
quests.textToSpeak: Okay, part of me wishes it were me. But when she held up that trophy, I was on my feet, shouting louder than anyone.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What comparison does the speaker make?
quests.explanation: The words say they're happy, but the comparison of time served shows envy is the real feeling.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm happy for her, I really am. It's just that she's been there six months, and I've been doing the same job for six years.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Focus on what the speaker says would have made the evening better.
quests.explanation: The politeness hides a let-down: the speaker hoped for his attention and didn't get it. Disappointment is the feeling here.
quests.textToSpeak: It was a lovely dinner, truly. I'd have enjoyed it more if he hadn't looked at his phone the entire time.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What has the speaker already done to prepare?
quests.explanation: Choosing a shirt and finding the bakery show the speaker is looking forward to it. So excited is the best fit.
quests.textToSpeak: First day at the new office tomorrow. I probably won't sleep. But I already know where the good bakery is, and I've picked out my shirt.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What does the speaker list after saying it's wonderful?
quests.explanation: The list of responsibilities shows a cautious unease about what's coming. That's what the clues add up to: apprehension.
quests.textToSpeak: We get the keys on Friday, which is wonderful, obviously. It's also two mortgages, one dog, and a boiler I don't understand.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What does the speaker's stomach do as time passes?
quests.explanation: The nearer the performance, the stronger the physical unease. That's nervousness.
quests.textToSpeak: We've been rehearsing for months, and it should be fine. Still, the closer we get to curtain up, the more my stomach does this thing.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What habit does the speaker describe, and what does it show?
quests.explanation: The relief is acknowledged, but the automatic habit of setting two cups shows how much the speaker misses her. Everything points to sadness.
quests.textToSpeak: Of course it's a relief that she's no longer in pain. I know that. But the house is so quiet, and I still set out two cups.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Which sentence carries more of the speaker's weight, the first or the second?
quests.explanation: Nostalgia is polite; the details about sleeping through the night show what the speaker feels most. This is relief.
quests.textToSpeak: I'll miss the place, obviously. Ten years is a long time. But I won't miss that leaking roof, and I can finally sleep through the night.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Are the two feelings the speaker mentions equal or one stronger?
quests.explanation: The speaker states two opposing feelings and can't choose. So conflicted is the best fit.
quests.textToSpeak: I can't decide whether to be glad or sorry. He's finally got what he wanted, and it means he'll be three thousand miles away.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What is the speaker replaying, and what do they wonder?
quests.explanation: Replaying conversations and wondering what changed shows hurt and loss rather than hostility. The speaker is sad.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm not angry with you. Really. I'm sitting here going over everything I said, wondering when you stopped wanting to tell me things.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What did the other person do in return for the speaker's help?
quests.explanation: The speaker denies sadness and lists the betrayals in a hard, accusing way. That's what the clues add up to: anger.
quests.textToSpeak: Sad? No. I'm not sad. I gave you three chances. I covered for you. And the first thing you did was tell the boss it was my idea to leave early.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What happens to the speech the speaker prepared?
quests.explanation: The anger was masking fear for him, and seeing him safe changes everything. The speaker is relieved.
quests.textToSpeak: I was so mad when he didn't call that I rehearsed what I'd say. Then he walked in, soaked, with a bandage on his hand, and I forgot every word.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What has the speaker been doing for an hour?
quests.explanation: Pride is mentioned, but standing at the window for an hour shows worry is the stronger feeling.
quests.textToSpeak: She passed her driving test, and I'm really proud, I am. But she took the car out alone at ten at night, and I've been standing at this window for an hour.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Consider what the speaker says they couldn't stop doing.
quests.explanation: The fussing shows a parent's nerves, but watching him with admiration is what the speaker dwells on. Pride is the feeling here.
quests.textToSpeak: He leaves for college on Sunday, and yes, I've packed his socks three times. But the way he stood at the door yesterday, so grown-up. I couldn't stop looking.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: How sure is the speaker about the outcome?
quests.explanation: The speaker leans toward a good outcome but can't be certain. This is hope.
quests.textToSpeak: I've made the call. I've said everything I needed to say. Now it's up to her. And I think, I really think, she'll say yes.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What can't the speaker do when the other person is nearby?
quests.explanation: Avoiding eye contact after asking for help shows discomfort about having needed to ask. That's embarrassment.
quests.textToSpeak: I know I shouldn't have asked. He handed me the money without a word, and now I can't look him in the eye. I'll pay it back by Friday.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: Which phrase does the speaker repeat?
quests.explanation: The fear is playful; the repeated 'I'm in' and the wish to commit show that excitement is winning.
quests.textToSpeak: The tickets say 'Row One,' and the ride's called 'The Drop.' I'm in. I'm absolutely in. Somebody hold my bag, and don't let me change my mind.

quests.instruction: Two feelings are in the mix. Which one comes through most strongly?
quests.hint: What does the speaker list as what they have?
quests.explanation: The speaker lists what they have and sounds settled, without regret. That's contentment.
quests.textToSpeak: It didn't work out, and honestly, I'm not sad. We wanted different things. I've got my friends, my job, and a very good sofa.
